correctness.rationale: The 14-site Fano incidence graph and prime-dimension state are explicitly normalized. Fourier-character orthogonality proves every reduced nonzero Schmidt eigenvalue equals p^{-r}, with p^r repetitions. Integer Smith reductions on all 1716 unordered cuts produce eleven exact factor classes, whose only prime divisors are 2 and 3. The 29 characteristic-three defects are exactly the point-line split plus 28 noncollinear-triangle splits; the latter have determinant magnitudes 3 and 2 on complementary subblocks, the canonical incidence matrix has determinant 24. Two independent exact Fano constructions and algorithms reproduce complete ranks, counts and geometry. The exhaustive nature of the finite proof is explicit; no infinite-graph conclusion is claimed.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is a canonical smallest incidence quantum network. The complete odd-prime balanced-cut entropy histogram identifies a physically meaningful exactly characterized arithmetic loss, linked to the 28 projective triangles rather than arbitrary labellings. Existing qubit cut data and general qudit rank tools do not provide these odd-prime numerical and geometric conclusions; the classification is a motivated exact finite benchmark with plausible use in qudit encoding and entanglement-resource comparison, without claiming a broader theorem.
